sources.title: GPT-5.6 Cyber — API model documentation
sources.evidence: Exact model ID and title; describes an alias for purpose-trained cybersecurity models requiring separate approval and provisioning. Lists 400,000-token context, 272,000 maximum input, 128,000 maximum output, text/image input, text output, reasoning tokens, function calling and Responses tools. Only the undated gpt-5.6-cyber identifier is listed as a snapshot. Fresh parameter re-audit on October 27 reopened the exact page through official documentation retrieval and the HTTP-200 Markdown fetched at 16:22 UTC; neither total nor activated parameters is listed.

sources.title: API changelog — August 7, 2026
sources.evidence: The August 7, 2026 feature entry names gpt-5.6-cyber and says Daybreak now offers separately approved access to purpose-trained models such as GPT-5.6 Cyber through Daybreak Red and the Responses API.

sources.title: Expanding Daybreak as the cyber defense window narrows
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. The August 10 announcement explicitly identifies GPT-5.6 Cyber as built on GPT-5.6 Sol and trained for specialized cybersecurity tasks and fewer refusals. This is named-base lineage, not merely family resemblance; the described changes concern training and behavior, with no pruning, distillation, expert expansion or new modality specified. No nominal total or active count is given for Cyber or its named base. The post still promises a later Cyber system card.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses accepts PDF file inputs. For vision-capable models the API extracts both document text and page images. This applies through the exact Cyber page listing image input and Responses support; it does not imply native PDF tokens or a distinct production modality encoder.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: The agreement provides limited nonexclusive access to business services and APIs, while section 9.1 reserves OpenAI intellectual-property rights. Together with separately approved hosted model access, this supports a descriptive Proprietary classification, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: All models
sources.evidence: Lists GPT-5.6 Cyber as a hosted model; the separately labeled open-weight section names gpt-oss models instead. No Cyber weights or open-weight license are offered here.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 System Card
sources.evidence: Fresh original PDF fetched October 27 at 15:42 UTC with HTTP 200; rechecked introduction, Model Data and Training, and full extracted text for counts and exact Cyber identity. The July 9 card (August 19 correction) covers Sol, Terra and Luna, not the later Cyber variant. It supplies no total or active count for the explicitly named Sol base from which a nominal Cyber count could be inferred.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card — Table 21
sources.evidence: Fresh original PDF fetched October 27 at 15:42 UTC with HTTP 200. Independently reopened Table 21 on printed page 110 and searched its full extracted text for parameter disclosures. The exact gpt-5.6-Cyber with Daybreak Red column contains defensive task completion percentages, not total or activated parameters. No count is established by this later original OpenAI comparison. A redundant web PDF fetch exceeded the web tool size limit; the successful original PDF cache was inspected.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: The current guide describes key/value intermediate states and distinct GPT-5.6-and-later cache behavior. The exact Cyber page lists prompt caching, but the guide does not explicitly identify Cyber as a Transformer or establish dense versus mixture-of-experts structure. KV caching alone is not used as architectural proof.

sources.title: How GPT-5.6 fuses frontier intelligence with frontier efficiency
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. The July 29 engineering article describes load balancing, sub-networks, kernels and a separate speculative draft model whose size/structure were experimentally changed. It publishes no numeric total or active count for Sol or Cyber. The separate draft, inference costs, token efficiency and one billion active users are not the target model parameter specification.

sources.title: Deprecations
sources.evidence: The complete current deprecation document was checked for the exact gpt-5.6-cyber identifier; no exact-model retirement entry was found. This does not test live endpoint operation.

sources.title: Attempted GPT-5.6 Cyber system-card PDF location
sources.evidence: The fresh October 27 original-source cache at 15:42 UTC and this dedicated re-audit web request both returned HTTP 404 at the conventional Cyber PDF URL. This is an unsuccessful lookup, not proof that no Cyber card exists elsewhere. Bounded exact-model system-card searches found the original launch post and later Astra comparison, not a count-bearing Cyber card.

sources.title: GPT-5.6 Sol — API model documentation
sources.evidence: Read the complete original Markdown fetched October 27 at 16:22 UTC with HTTP 200. The exact named Cyber base is GPT-5.6 Sol; its model page identifies the model and aliases and lists context, modalities, API features and prices, but no nominal total or active parameters. The valid Cyber-to-Sol lineage therefore has no supported numeric base count to inherit.

sources.title: GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27. The July 9 family launch identifies Sol, Terra and Luna as model tiers and provides performance, latency, cost and multi-agent comparisons, without numeric total or active model counts. Four- and sixteen-agent settings are inference orchestration, not model parameter counts; qualitative size tiers do not establish a nominal count for the Sol base.

name.note: Exact display name in the official model documentation and announcement.

family.note: The exact model identifier is gpt-5.6-cyber; the announcement explicitly identifies GPT-5.6 Sol as its base. Replace the overly broad gpt family.

release_date.note: Retain August 7: the dated API changelog explicitly offers Cyber through separately approved Daybreak Red. August 10 is the later public announcement. Earlier customer previews mentioned without dates do not establish an earlier public release.

open_weights.note: Hosted, separately approved Daybreak access; the official catalog distinguishes its open-weight models and does not offer Cyber weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted service under OpenAI terms; no Cyber open-weight distribution license is documented.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit reopened the exact API page and launch, Sol API/family launch and system card, engineering article, and later Astra comparison. Cyber is explicitly built on Sol with specialized training; the described changes do not identify structural compression or expansion, so nominal lineage inference is admissible in principle. However, no supported total is published for either Cyber or Sol. Bounded exact Cyber/Sol searches for parameters, billion/trillion scales and technical reports found no count-bearing original specification. This null reflects absent nominal evidence, not a demand for a tensor census or production attestation.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-model searches separately checked active/activated parameters and later original research comparison columns. Astra Table 21 identifies Cyber exactly but reports completion percentages only; the Sol and Cyber sources give no nominal active count to disclose or inherit. No count-bearing original model-team comparison was located. Draft-model experiments, multi-agent settings, hardware/cost and behavioral capacity estimates are not active-count specifications; no dense-equals-active inference is made.

architecture.note: Exact production structure remains unverified. The announcement explicitly establishes derivation from Sol, but checked first-party sources do not establish Sol or Cyber topology. Current KV caching, generic sub-networks and speculative draft-model experiments are insufficient. Older pre-GPT-5.6 caching descriptions are not used. A separate Cyber card was not located; the attempted PDF URL returned 404.

context_window.note: Current exact-model documentation states 400,000 total context, maximum input 272,000 and maximum output 128,000. A generic pricing line for longer prompts is not taken as evidence of a larger input limit. Documented specification, not a live endpoint test.

modalities.note: Native documented input is text/image and output is text. Add PDF as a supported Responses input format: the API converts PDFs into extracted text and page images for this explicitly vision-capable model. Hosted image-generation tools do not imply native image output; no audio/video input is documented.

reasoning.note: Exact model page explicitly supports reasoning tokens; the announcement discusses Cyber reasoning budgets. No unsupported reasoning-effort enum is inferred.

tool_call.note: Exact model page explicitly lists function_calling and Responses tools including web/file search, code interpreter, hosted shell, apply_patch, skills, computer use, MCP and tool search. Chat Completions is not supported.

description.value: Cybersecurity model for authorized vulnerability research and security testing
description.note: Retain the factual description; it matches the documented authorized defensive scope without comparative marketing claims. Access restrictions are recorded in notes.

patch.notes: Released through separately approved Daybreak Red access on August 7, 2026; the announcement followed on August 10. GPT-5.6 Cyber is an undated alias for purpose-trained cybersecurity models, built on GPT-5.6 Sol, and requires separate approval and provisioning. Current documentation lists 400,000 total context, 272,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output, with reasoning tokens, function calling and Responses tools; Chat Completions is unsupported. PDF is an API input format converted to extracted text and page images, not evidence of a native PDF encoder. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed after the October 27 recheck. Cyber has explicit Sol lineage, but no supported nominal Sol count is available to inherit; the later Astra comparison reports performance only. Production architecture remains unverified. Only the undated model alias is listed, no exact deprecation was found in the current deprecation document, and endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter-only re-audit retains undisclosed total and active counts after reopening exact Cyber evidence, its explicitly named Sol base, original family and later Astra cards, and bounded new disclosure/comparison searches. Named Sol lineage is acceptable in principle, but neither model has a supported nominal count to inherit. Explicit null patches include both counts and parameters_source; the other 12 field assessments are unchanged.
